subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core accept this PR's `gateway.peers` and raw `gatewayUrl` cross-gateway session-tool routing, or defer/rework it behind a maintainer-approved federation and peer-trust contract?
rationale: This changes gateway trust boundaries, model-callable URL routing, credentials, session ownership, and message delivery semantics; automation cannot choose that product/security boundary safely.

options.title: Rework Behind Explicit Peer Trust
options.body: Define allowlisted peer identity, auth, idempotency/replay, URL policy, and session visibility first, then update the PR to match that contract.

options.title: Defer To Federation FRD
options.body: Leave this PR open or close it later after https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 resolves the broader bridge protocol and identity model.

options.title: Accept Experimental Core Routing
options.body: Maintainership can intentionally own the new risk, but the patch still needs the blocking protocol/security fixes and live two-gateway proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Rework Behind Explicit Peer Trust
recommendation.body: Define allowlisted peer identity, auth, idempotency/replay, URL policy, and session visibility first, then update the PR to match that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest available recent history across the session-tool and gateway/protocol surfaces that frame this decision.
